THE PHYSICS

Q̇ = H(T₁ − T₂)

Energy lost by one block is gained by the other. Their final temperature depends on both heat capacities. Greater conductance speeds up equilibration without changing the final temperature.

TRY AN EXPERIMENT

Unequal heat capacities

Give the cold block twice the mass of the hot block. Predict whether the final temperature is above or below 50°C.

Inside this model +

Two uniform copper blocks with constant specific heat 385 J/(kg·K), connected by constant thermal conductance H and insulated from surroundings. No phase changes or temperature gradients within a block. Temperatures approach equilibrium continuously; time is accelerated 10× at the 1× playback setting.

C₁ dT₁/dt = −H(T₁ − T₂); C₂ dT₂/dt = +H(T₁ − T₂). Teq = (C₁T₁₀ + C₂T₂₀)/(C₁ + C₂); ΔT decays as exp[−H(1/C₁ + 1/C₂)t].
